issues.detail: The Greek 'ουκ επεγινωσκον την γην' means 'they did not recognize the land'. The Vietnamese translation 'không nhận biết đất' omits the object 'land' (γην) or treats it as a general lack of recognition, but more importantly, the Greek structure implies they didn't recognize the land [as a place to land], whereas the Vietnamese phrasing is slightly ambiguous.

The Greek 'κολπον δε τινα κατενοουν εχοντα αιγιαλον' means 'but they saw [no] bay having a beach'. The Vietnamese translation 'thấy một cái lòng có bờ biển' translates this as an affirmative ('saw a bay with a beach'), whereas the Greek 'ουκ' (not) at the beginning of the sentence governs the entire clause, meaning they did NOT see any bay with a beach.
